Source: He has a history of diabetes, obesity, and hypertension but does not see a physician for his underlying conditions.
A 59-year-old man presents to the emergency department after a sudden onset of slurred speech and right upper extremity weakness.
Physical exam reveals normal vision, strength, and sensation with a stable gait.
His symptoms lasted 20 minutes but by the time he arrived at the emergency department he was symptom-free.
A CT scan of the head is performed and is unremarkable.
The patient denies any preceding symptoms.
Finger-nose testing and tandem gait are unremarkable.
His temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air.
